_readme: Mutation evidence a target's acceptance quotes, kept executable (🎯T32).
A target's acceptance says 'reintroducing X makes test T RED'. That sentence
is quoted once, in a commit message, and then never re-run. Any later commit
that changes T's inputs can retire the evidence without turning anything red:
🎯T30's 8c5e04a added a `landed` argument to ensureSubmitted and passed
landed=true at 🎯T28's call sites, which was correct for the branch it modelled
and weakened no assertion — but it made 🎯T28's over-broadness mutation stop
biting TestT28DailyDeliveredFramesReportSuccess. Every suite stayed green.
This file is the machine-readable form of those sentences, and
scripts/check-mutation-evidence.py re-derives them: `make verify-mutation-evidence`,
run in CI. Each entry names the target, the mutation as an anchored source edit,
and the tests that must go RED (and the ones that must stay GREEN) under it.
The same Makefile target also runs the check with --prove-teeth, which is what
keeps THIS check from becoming the next unwired oracle: an entry may declare a
`decay`, and --prove-teeth asserts that applying it leaves every suite green
(so CI sees nothing) while making a `red` test survive the mutation (so this
check, and only this check, goes red).
TO ADD AN ENTRY when you quote mutation evidence in a commit body:
target    the target whose acceptance quotes it
mutation  a stable id for this mutation, unique within the target
what      one line: what the mutation reintroduces or removes
quoted_by the commit whose message quotes this evidence
package   the Go package the tests live in
edits     [{file, find, replace}] — `find` must occur EXACTLY ONCE in file.
Anchor text, not a diff hunk: a hunk decays on the first refactor
of its context. When the anchor stops matching the check goes RED
and says so, which is the point — the mutation must be re-derived
by a human, never silently skipped.
tests     [{name, expect}] — name is a `go test` path, so a subtest is
'TestX/subtest_name'. expect is 'red' (the mutation must kill it)
or 'green' (it must survive — that is how a commit body's
'fixture Y stays green under this mutation, so the two cover
distinct mechanisms' claim stays true).
decay     optional {what, models, edits} — an edit to the TESTS' inputs,
modelled on a real commit, that disarms this evidence without
turning any suite red. --prove-teeth applies it and requires
exactly that: green everywhere on its own, and a `red` test
surviving the mutation once both are applied. Worth declaring
for any entry whose evidence has decayed once already.
note      optional prose: provenance, or what decayed here before.

entries.what: Agent.Send drops the provider's error and returns nil, the swallow that made a lost submit invisible above agent.go
entries.note: 2017074 also quoted TestClaudeSendReportsUnsubmittedTurnThroughRealTmux against this mutation. It is not listed here because it skips without tmux and a skipped test is not evidence; the hermetic one holds the contract in every environment.

entries.what: MatchTurnInProgress forgets Claude Code's activity line, so a running turn with a drained composer reads as no chrome at all

decay.what: the Send-level call site passes landed=true, so sawContent starts true and 🎯T30's composerEmptyIdle branch returns nil before the 🎯T28 classification is consulted at all
decay.models: 8c5e04a, which did this to TestT28DailyDeliveredFramesReportSuccess: correct for the paste branch that test models, no assertion weakened, every suite green, and the caller-visible half of 🎯T28's evidence gone

entries.note: This is the entry 🎯T32 was filed over. aa71680 quoted TestT28DailyDeliveredFramesReportSuccess/frame_daily_spinner_empty_composer.txt as the caller-visible RED half. 8c5e04a passed landed=true at that call site and the subtest went green under the mutation, leaving only the classifier half biting; 9944f39 restored the contract on the landed=false path as TestT28DeliveredFramesReportSuccessWithoutLandedEvidence, which is what this entry names. The green expectation is aa71680's own distinctness claim: the queued frame is the half 2017074 already closed, so the two fixtures cover different mechanisms rather than doubling up.

entries.what: classifyComposer forgets Claude Code's queued-messages hint, so a payload accepted behind a running turn stops counting as submitted
MatchUnsubmittedPaste asks whether the composer was DRAWN rather than whether it HOLDS anything, the pre-fix predicate that reported delivered sends as stuck chips
maybeContinueGoal stops calling Send, so an open Goal dies after one terminal turn
